chapter: Jimmy Butts, Doc Pittman and women in jazz
title: Staying focused through distractions, church bells in Italian squares
summary: She tells students to ignore distractions, recalling Italian village-square concerts interrupted by steeple bells.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Yeah. I try too. I try to let my students know that they can’t get distracted when a baby cries or somebody screams or you get these strange things happening in the audience, or a fire engine. It takes a lot of discipline to do that. In Italy of course we play in the village squares a lot in the summer. And at 9 or 10:00 sharp, right in the middle of a tune, bong- bong. You know? From the steeple.
Try to work that into your solo.
Sometimes nature takes care of it and it just fits right in.
